passage.title: Cool Roofs
passage.prompt: Explain one benefit of a cool roof. Use evidence from the passage to support your answer.
passage.text:
On a summer afternoon, a dark roof can become much hotter than the air around it. Dark surfaces absorb most of the sunlight that hits them and turn it into heat. Some of that heat moves down into the rooms below, so people run fans and air conditioners longer.

A cool roof is covered with a light-colored or reflective coating. Instead of absorbing most of the sunlight, it reflects much of it back toward the sky. In a fictional town described here, workers coated the roof of a small library. The staff reported that the reading room felt more comfortable in July, and the building used less electricity for cooling than it had the summer before.

Cool roofs are not perfect. In places with long, cold winters, a roof that stays cooler can mean a building needs a little more heating. Coatings also get dirty and must be cleaned or replaced. Planners compare these costs with the benefits before choosing a roof.

R01.text: One benefit of a cool roof is that it keeps the building cooler inside. The passage says a cool roof "reflects much of it back toward the sky" instead of absorbing it. Because less sunlight turns into heat, less heat moves down into the rooms, so people do not need to run air conditioners as long.
